<!-- adguard-filters-agent:report {"schemaVersion":1,"revisionDigest":"c89754740435dcff4c48f83f371270d4fafaee321bd6c3303e2263e1c070a716"} -->
Analysis-only findings, no verified change

## Reproduced symptom

Indeterminate — Filtering leaves GlasgowLive's blocked top billboard as an empty 1000x260 sticky white strip that pushes the site header down 260px and swallows left clicks on headline links beneath it (elementFromPoint at the teaser link returns the strip), matching the reporter's "left click does not navigate". A site-scoped cosmetic rule hiding that leftover strip was visually verified as resolving it with page integrity intact, but the apply_rule environment refused both selector forms, so the rule is attached for a maintainer instead of being proposed.

## Candidate for review

`glasgowlive.co.uk##body > div:has(> .commercial-box-child-style)`

BaseFilter/sections/specific.txt

Not verified: apply_rule refused both forms. This one returned baseline_symptom_absent:⁠ the site paints the same emptied billboard wrapper (1000x260, white, position:⁠sticky, z-index 9998, holding .commercial-box-child-style ⁠> .commercial-gpt-style) on the unfiltered page too, only its content differs, so the harness could not separate filtered from unfiltered and ran no visual review. The equivalent glasgowlive.co.uk#⁠#⁠div.sticky:⁠has(⁠> .commercial-box-child-style) did get a bound visual review that verified it (symptom resolved, pageIntegrity intact, adLayoutResidue absent, remainingInstances empty, observedDamage empty) but its environmentExperiment failed candidate_phase_symptom, which the contract reads as the symptom still there, so it cannot be carried. The body ⁠> div form is preferred because one observed load applied no sticky class, on which div.sticky matches nothing.

## Executor and version

Pinned prebuilt release v5.5.2.3

## Artifacts

https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/actions/runs/42434758286

comment.body:
Candidate rule proposed ## Reproduced symptom Reproduced — On www⁠.tour.ne.jp the reporter's annotation marks the site's own social share buttons (`sns-share-btn`), which leave an almost empty grey-share-icon band between the author card and the related-tags section. Adding `tour.ne.jp##.sns-share-btn` to the Social filter hid both share buttons with the page intact and no residue, confirmed by the browser experiment and vision review. ## Rule `tour.ne.jp##.sns-share-btn` ## Policy rationale The report is a social-widget leftover, which is neither first-party advertising, a paywall, nor a German anti-adblock wall, so none of the run instruction's closing rules applies. There is no anti-adblock wall on the page, so the anti-adblock gate does not apply. The AdGuard Social filter's stated purpose covers 'Share' buttons on third-party sites, and its exceptions (comments, embedded posts, polls, login widgets, links to the site's social pages) do not cover this share control. ## Place in the list [SocialFilter/sections/specific.txt](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/d33bf95a3b5d74aedcc3e19163260eb82ba9a9e4/SocialFilter/sections/specific.txt) By adding the domain to the existing rule on [line 8546](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/d33bf95a3b5d74aedcc3e19163260eb82ba9a9e4/SocialFilter/sections/specific.txt#L8546). ## Screenshots
Without and with the rule | Without the rule | With the rule | |---|---| | | |

## Reproduced symptom

Indeterminate — On carpet-rug.org the Cookie Notices filter's generic rule #⁠#⁠#⁠gdpr-cookie-consent-bar hides the GDPR Cookie Consent bar, leaving the plugin's empty full-viewport modal plus black backdrop over the whole page so nothing can be clicked and the cookie-gated video never unlocks. A site-scoped trusted-click-element rule on #⁠cookie_action_accept_all removes that overlay and loads the YouTube player (phase-C viewport shows the player, page integrity intact, no ad residue), but the review rejected it only because tiled full-page captures paint every cross-origin YouTube iframe as a black rectangle, which I reproduced in an unfiltered browser.

<!-- adguard-filters-agent:report {"schemaVersion":1,"revisionDigest":"119d17e73a50ab35aef35208255882477e50d035b522c4203efc0389744394b6"} -->
Analysis-only findings, no verified change

## Reproduced symptom

Indeterminate — Issue #⁠246612 is a real leftover:⁠ five empty `div.ad-slot-root` gpt containers reserve 250px of blank space each on www⁠.ilfoglio.it because the ad scripts are already blocked. The proposed rule `ilfoglio.it##.ad-slot-root` was applied and removed all ad reservation with the page intact, but the vision review refused it for blank regions that measured checks prove are unloaded lazy article photos and a first-party "IL FOGLIO ON AIR" promo, not ad space, so it reaches a human unverified.

## Still visible after the rule

- Bottom viewport, over the three-teaser row beneath the Trump/Ukraine lead story — Floating dark 'IL FOGLIO ON AIR' / 'Il Foglio, ora anche video.' promotional banner with an ON AIR badge and a 'VAI AL PALINSESTO' button overlays article text at the bottom of the viewport; it is a visible special-banner/ad overlay, not blank space.
- Right-hand column below the article 'L’elzeviro di Fini:⁠ “La sinistra che festeggia per Trump, poi perde in Italia. È rimasta yankee go home”' — Large empty white reserved advertising region occupying the right column from below the Fini article to the bottom of the tile; no creative, ad label, frame, or placeholder block is visible inside it.
- Le false minacce sugli aerei ci ricordano che sulla cybersicurezza la politica non si può più dividere / Tajani:⁠ "Diffusi i miei dati personali sul dark web" — Large empty white reserved ad-slot region above this article teaser; no ad creative, label, frame, iframe, or placeholder block is visible inside it.
- L’ex presidente della Republika Srpska a Mar-a-Lago — right-hand side of the lead image — Large reserved white rectangle beside the Dodik article image; no ad creative, REKLAMA label, frame, or placeholder is rendered in it, consistent with an empty leftover ad slot.
- La notizia che non c’è:⁠ i cattolici non hanno votato Trump / I prossimi regali di Trump ai dem — right-hand column — Tall blank white column to the right of the bottom article list; no ad creative, label, frame, or placeholder is visible, consistent with leftover empty ad-slot area.
- and 1 more of the same, in the run artifacts

## Executor and version

Pinned prebuilt release v5.5.2.3

## Missing information

- Full-page capture does not trigger loading="lazy" article images, so the vision review reads their reserved boxes as leftover ad space: On www⁠.ilfoglio.it (1920x19961 page) 45 of 46 article images carry loading="lazy". In the live session only 6 image requests were made (artifact:⁠har:⁠76e31611-af1f-42a3-bc1b-2b7a5eec37bd), and evaluate_js reports 40 lazy <⁠img⁠> elements not yet loaded reserving \~14,656 px of box height, none of them inside an ad slot; 39 of the 46 images were also incomplete at the time of the first full-page capture. The apply_rule full-page tiles therefore show large white rectangles in article columns, and both vision reviews classified them as "large empty white reserved ad regions" (and once as "non-target rendering damage"). Scrolling the page in interact_page reduces the incomplete count only slightly, and the tiled capture itself never forces those images to load. What is missing is a capture mode (or a required reveal step) that forces lazy resources to load before the full-page capture, so a "blank space" that is really an unloaded article photo is not scored as an ad leftover or as page damage.

issue.title: facebook.com: sponsored-post #%# MutationObserver rules in Base filter cause severe main-thread jank (~10 s per page load)
issue.body:
### Prerequisites
- [x] This site DOES NOT contain sexually explicit material
- [x] Filters were updated before reproducing an issue (Base filter 2.5.2.64, updated 2026-11-06)
- [x] AdGuard product version is up-to-date
- [x] Browser version is up-to-date
- [x] Disabling the JS rules on the site resolves the issue

### What product do you use?
AdGuard Browser Extension

### AdGuard version
5.5.3.49 (MV3)

### What type of problem have you encountered?
Website or app doesn't work properly (severe slowness / freezing)

### Which browser(s) do you use?
Chrome 157.0.8103.38

### Which device do you use?
Desktop (Windows 11, Intel i7-1185G7, 32 GB RAM, the machine itself is idle)

### Where is the problem encountered?
https://www.facebook.com/ (feed, groups and single post pages)

### What filters do you have enabled?
- Ad Blocking: AdGuard Base filter
- Other: AdGuard Search Ads and Self-Promotion filter, EasyList Hebrew

### Issue details

Facebook is constantly slow and freezes while loading and scrolling. I profiled it with Chrome DevTools (performance trace + CPU profile) and found that almost all of the extra main-thread time comes from the facebook.com `#%#` JS rules in AdGuard Base filter that hide sponsored posts.

These rules create a `MutationObserver` on `document` with `{childList: true, subtree: true}`. On every mutation the callback runs `document.querySelectorAll()` with a very large selector list (`div[data-pagelet^="FeedUnit"]…`, `div[role="feed"] > div…`, `#ssrb_feed_start + div …`, and so on) and inspects `__reactFiber` props on the results. Facebook mutates the DOM constantly, so the callback runs hundreds of times while the page loads and keeps running during scrolling. The callback is not throttled or debounced.

**Measured on the same post page, with a MutationObserver wrapper injected before page scripts to time each observer callback:**

| | Before | After adding `@@\|\|facebook.com^$jsinject` |
|---|---|---|
| DOMContentLoaded | 15.0 s / 16.9 s (one run > 60 s) | **3.3 s / 2.4 s** |
| load event | 18.3 s / 64 s | **4.2 s / 2.7 s** |
| Time spent in AdGuard observer callbacks | **~11.4 s** | 0 |
| Time spent in all page MutationObservers | > 11.4 s | 0.13–0.25 s |

Breakdown of the observer callbacks before the fix (one page load):

| Rule (AdGuard Base filter) | Calls | Total time | Max single call |
|---|---|---|---|
| Feed sponsored posts: `!function(){var b=0,d=[];new MutationObserver(function(){document.querySelectorAll("div[data-pagelet^=\"FeedUnit\"]…, div[role=\"feed\"] > span…, #ssrb_feed_start + div > div[class]…` | 569 | **10,396 ms** | 100 ms |
| Sidebar (`div[role="complementary"]`, `__reactFiber`): `(()=>{const e=new MutationObserver((()=>{const n=document.querySelectorAll('div[role="complementary"] …` | 569 | 911 ms | 9 ms |
| Old interface (`div[id^='mount_']` / `hyperfeed_story_id` / `socheck`) | 569 | 119 ms | 2 ms |

In the CPU profile, `querySelectorAll` called from these callbacks accounted for ~10 s of self time out of ~26 s of main-thread activity. All other extensions together used under 0.3 s.

**Suggestions**
- Debounce or throttle the observer callback (for example, collect mutations and process them once per `requestAnimationFrame` or `requestIdleCallback`).
- Query only the added nodes (`mutation.addedNodes`) instead of re-running the full-document `querySelectorAll` on every mutation.
- Drop the selectors for the old Facebook interface (`hyperfeed_story_id`, `userContentWrapper`), which no longer exists.

**Workaround:** the user rule `@@||facebook.com^$jsinject` removes the freeze completely, at the cost of some sponsored posts coming back.

Analysis-only findings, no verified change

## Reproduced symptom

Indeterminate — The report's premise is real:⁠ AdGuard Base filter ships 12 facebook.com-scoped `#%#` JS rules, including the sponsored-post MutationObserver rule the reporter quotes, applied on every facebook.com load. The reported defect is main-thread jank on a logged-in feed, which this run could not reach (both facebook.com URLs showed a sign-in wall) and which no filter-list rule can fix, so a maintainer rewrite of those rule bodies is needed; the only filter-expressible lever is carried, not endorsed.

## Candidate for review

BaseFilter/sections/allowlist.txt

Not verified: Carried for a human decision, not endorsed. The symptom is a main-thread timing defect on a logged-in Facebook feed; this run reached only a sign-in wall on two facebook.com URLs (full-page vision:⁠ sign_in_wall, reporterSymptomPresence indeterminate, instanceCount 0), so the \~10.4 s observer cost and the candidate's effect on it could not be measured, and apply_rule's screenshot phases cannot judge timing. The rule is a domain-wide unblock:⁠ 12 Base-filter `#%#` rules are scoped to facebook.com (sponsored feed posts, complementary sidebar, watch, marketplace), so this exception disables all of them and brings those ads back, against the policy that unblocking rules be as specific as possible; no `$jsinject` rule exists in this repository, so the path is a guess. The real fix is a maintainer rewrite of the existing `#%#` rule bodies, which no filter-list rule can express.

## Executor and version

Pinned prebuilt release v5.5.2.3

## Missing information

- Run instruction has no policy for reports about performance cost of existing filter rules: The run instruction's filter policy lists close/no-rule cases (first-party ads, paywalls, German anti-adblock walls, other anti-adblock without a captured detector) and maintainer rules for anti-adblock popups and shared rules, but says nothing about a report whose defect is the runtime performance cost of already-shipped filter rules (here:⁠ facebook.com `#%#` MutationObserver rules in Base filter). It is therefore undefined whether such a report should be closed, handed to a maintainer, or answered with an unblocking exception such as `@@||facebook.com^$jsinject`, and which of those the outcome type must express.

issue.title: facebook.com: sponsored-post #%# MutationObserver rules in Base filter cause severe main-thread jank (~10 s per page load)
issue.body:
### Prerequisites
- [x] This site DOES NOT contain sexually explicit material
- [x] Filters were updated before reproducing an issue (Base filter 2.5.2.64, updated 2026-11-06)
- [x] AdGuard product version is up-to-date
- [x] Browser version is up-to-date
- [x] Disabling the JS rules on the site resolves the issue

### What product do you use?
AdGuard Browser Extension

### AdGuard version
5.5.3.49 (MV3)

### What type of problem have you encountered?
Website or app doesn't work properly (severe slowness / freezing)

### Which browser(s) do you use?
Chrome 157.0.8103.38

### Which device do you use?
Desktop (Windows 11, Intel i7-1185G7, 32 GB RAM, the machine itself is idle)

### Where is the problem encountered?
https://www.facebook.com/ (feed, groups and single post pages)

### What filters do you have enabled?
- Ad Blocking: AdGuard Base filter
- Other: AdGuard Search Ads and Self-Promotion filter, EasyList Hebrew

### Issue details

Facebook is constantly slow and freezes while loading and scrolling. I profiled it with Chrome DevTools (performance trace + CPU profile) and found that almost all of the extra main-thread time comes from the facebook.com `#%#` JS rules in AdGuard Base filter that hide sponsored posts.

These rules create a `MutationObserver` on `document` with `{childList: true, subtree: true}`. On every mutation the callback runs `document.querySelectorAll()` with a very large selector list (`div[data-pagelet^="FeedUnit"]…`, `div[role="feed"] > div…`, `#ssrb_feed_start + div …`, and so on) and inspects `__reactFiber` props on the results. Facebook mutates the DOM constantly, so the callback runs hundreds of times while the page loads and keeps running during scrolling. The callback is not throttled or debounced.

**Measured on the same post page, with a MutationObserver wrapper injected before page scripts to time each observer callback:**

| | Before | After adding `@@\|\|facebook.com^$jsinject` |
|---|---|---|
| DOMContentLoaded | 15.0 s / 16.9 s (one run > 60 s) | **3.3 s / 2.4 s** |
| load event | 18.3 s / 64 s | **4.2 s / 2.7 s** |
| Time spent in AdGuard observer callbacks | **~11.4 s** | 0 |
| Time spent in all page MutationObservers | > 11.4 s | 0.13–0.25 s |

Breakdown of the observer callbacks before the fix (one page load):

| Rule (AdGuard Base filter) | Calls | Total time | Max single call |
|---|---|---|---|
| Feed sponsored posts: `!function(){var b=0,d=[];new MutationObserver(function(){document.querySelectorAll("div[data-pagelet^=\"FeedUnit\"]…, div[role=\"feed\"] > span…, #ssrb_feed_start + div > div[class]…` | 569 | **10,396 ms** | 100 ms |
| Sidebar (`div[role="complementary"]`, `__reactFiber`): `(()=>{const e=new MutationObserver((()=>{const n=document.querySelectorAll('div[role="complementary"] …` | 569 | 911 ms | 9 ms |
| Old interface (`div[id^='mount_']` / `hyperfeed_story_id` / `socheck`) | 569 | 119 ms | 2 ms |

In the CPU profile, `querySelectorAll` called from these callbacks accounted for ~10 s of self time out of ~26 s of main-thread activity. All other extensions together used under 0.3 s.

**Suggestions**
- Debounce or throttle the observer callback (for example, collect mutations and process them once per `requestAnimationFrame` or `requestIdleCallback`).
- Query only the added nodes (`mutation.addedNodes`) instead of re-running the full-document `querySelectorAll` on every mutation.
- Drop the selectors for the old Facebook interface (`hyperfeed_story_id`, `userContentWrapper`), which no longer exists.

**Workaround:** the user rule `@@||facebook.com^$jsinject` removes the freeze completely, at the cost of some sponsored posts coming back.

Candidate rule proposed ## Reproduced symptom Reproduced — The reporter's outlined defect on www⁠.tozlu.com is the site's own fixed cookie-consent card ("Çerez tercihleriniz" with accept/reject/settings), served in the page HTML with no consent-vendor request behind it. Hiding its stable component class with tozlu.com#⁠#⁠.ms-cerez-bandi verified in the A/B/C experiment (card visible in baseline, hidden with the candidate, page integrity intact, no remaining instances) and belongs in the AdGuard Cookie Notices filter. ## Rule `tozlu.com##.ms-cerez-bandi` ## Policy rationale The report is a cookie-notice annoyance, which belongs to an AdGuard annoyance filter; no policy rule in the run instruction closes it (it is not the site's first-party advertising, not a paywall, and not an anti-adblock wall). The reporter-defined target is the site's own cookie-consent card, and the fix is a standard domain-scoped element-hiding rule for the AdGuard Cookie Notices filter. ## Place in the list [AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/e77d38af4b45a575844946c48c70bf43f78c89b3/AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt) At the end of the file. ## Screenshots

comment.body:
Candidate rule proposed ## Reproduced symptom Reproduced — mebelplyt.pl (PrestaShop shop using the first-party 'seigicookie' module built on the orestbida cookieconsent library) still shows its centered "Używamy ciasteczek!" consent dialog under the reporter's setup, whose Cookie Notices filter is enabled. The fix is to add mebelplyt.pl to the existing shared cookieconsent element-hiding rule `…,rsd.cz###cc_div` in AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt; the domain-scoped form was validated with apply_rule (symptom resolved, page integrity intact). ## Rule `mebelplyt.pl###cc_div` ## Executor and version Pinned prebuilt release v5.5.2.3 ## Policy rationale The report is a cookie-consent annoyance, not first-party advertising, a paywall, an anti-adblock wall, or a scam/phishing page, so none of the run instruction's closing rules applies. The reported element is a removable overlay whose serving request is visible (first-party /modules/seigicookie/…), and the fix belongs to the AdGuard Cookie Notices filter's existing shared cookieconsent rule family, which the run instruction says to extend rather than duplicate. ## Place in the list [AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/e77d38af4b45a575844946c48c70bf43f78c89b3/AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt) By adding the domain to the existing rule on [line 7795](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/e77d38af4b45a575844946c48c70bf43f78c89b3/AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt#L7795). ## Screenshots

The reported defect was not reproduced

## Reproduced symptom

Indeterminate — The site's first-party ad-block detector (忍者AdMax tag v1.0.0 in /js/lsf-support.js) did execute, but its bait and network probes are already neutralised by the existing ff14-tools.com rules in BaseFilter/sections/antiadblock.txt, and full-page vision of three successful loads shows the reported overlay absent, so closing as not reproduced is recommended.

## Policy rationale

The run instruction's policy does not block a rule here:⁠ this is a non-German anti-adblock wall and the captured requests do show the detector script (first-party https:⁠//ff14-tools.com/js/lsf-support.js plus its adm.shinobi.jp/abd.js probes), so rule generation was permitted. The close recommendation rests on non-reproduction, not on a policy rule:⁠ the reported anti-adblock overlay was absent on every successful load of the reported URL with the reporter's filter selection, confirmed by session-bound full-page vision (reporterSymptomPresence absent).
